resources.string: How heavy the pedals feel overall. Above 100% the trainer brakes harder, below it less. The speed of the ride on the route does not change.
How clearly gravel, forest floor and grass can be felt compared with asphalt. 100% is today’s table, 0% feels the same everywhere.
Default: 100% — how the app calculates today.
Ride steadily for 2–3 minutes; the app suggests an overall resistance.
A real trainer must be paired for this (not the demo trainer).
What the trainer was given and what came out — on this device only.
Pedal steadily for 2–3 minutes on a flat stretch: about 80–90 rpm, calm, without shifting. The app compares your power with what a bike needs on the flat.
Get going: at least 100 watts and 60–110 rpm.
Settling in … %1$d seconds until the measurement starts.
Measuring — keep pedalling steadily. %1$d seconds left.
Measured %1$d W at %2$d rpm; expected for a bike on the flat: %3$d W. Accuracy of the factor roughly ±%4$d%%.
The calculated value was outside the limits (70–130%) and was capped.
Accepted. Applies from the next ride; it can be reset under Ride feel at any time.
A flat stretch shows the resistance only roughly. After accepting, ride a few times and adjust if needed; the ride log helps with that.
Too few usable readings. Keep at least 100 watts at 60–110 rpm the whole time.
The power was too low for a reliable measurement (under 100 watts).
The cadence was outside 60–110 rpm. Pick a gear that gives about 85 rpm.
Power or cadence was too uneven or drifted. Try again and pedal steadily.
The speed of the ride did not match your power — probably the ride had not settled yet. Please try again.
The gear was changed. Stay in one gear and try again.
The result would be far outside the usual (more than half to double the resistance). That points to a measurement error, so nothing is suggested.
One line every 5 seconds per ride: set grade or resistance, measured power, simulated speed, gear. The files stay on this device; only what you share yourself leaves it. At most 12 rides are kept.
No log yet. One is created on every ride.
Only the first %1$d lines are shown here; the whole file is shared.
